story: At 9:17 on a humid, hazy Saturday morning in Sumter Oaks, Gary is measuring and marking spots on his golf cart for lights and a speaker, though nothing gets drilled yet. Donna is packing paddles, balls, and water bottles for her pickleball game with Gary on court one, while Hal settles into his porch chair with a cup of coffee to watch the quiet street. Over at Rosa's kitchen, she keeps prepping the main dish for tonight's dinner, and everyone is buzzing a little about the new Halloween on the Loop flyer, with its golf cart parade and costume contest on October 31.
events: Town news: A flyer went up on the Magnolia Loop bulletin board: Halloween on the Loop, Saturday, October 31. Trick-or-treating from 5 to 7 PM, a golf cart parade around the Loop at 6, then a costume contest at the Town Square bandstand at 7, with prizes for best costume and best-decorated golf cart. Decorations welcome all week.
Gary (gary golf cart): Measure and mark mounting spots for lights and speaker, no drilling, nothing installed yet
Donna (donna pickleball bag): Pack paddles, balls, and water bottles for court one with Gary
Hal (hal porch chair): Sit on the porch with a cup of coffee and watch the quiet street
Rosa (rosa kitchen): Keep prepping the main dish for tonight's dinner

gary.thought_process: The application is filed and I've already bench-fit the bracket and tested the light strip and speaker wiring indoors. Nothing goes on the cart until the review board approves, per L-01, and nothing amplified, but there's still prep I can do inside. It's a quiet Saturday morning and I don't have to be at Rosa's until five. Time to look over the cart itself, plan where the lights and speaker will mount, and measure so installation goes quick once approval comes through.

parameters.content: Measure and mark mounting spots for lights and speaker, no drilling, nothing installed yet

donna.thought_process: It's 9:17 AM Saturday and I'm home alone. The plan is court one with Gary this afternoon and the cobbler and ice cream for Rosa's at five. Nobody is nearby to talk to, and I've already checked the calendar twice, so I won't check it a third time. The useful thing is to get my gear ready so I can go straight to the court. My pickleball bag is right here, so I'll pack it with paddles, balls, and water for the footwork session with Gary. Then I'll start on the cobbler prep.

parameters.content: Pack paddles, balls, and water bottles for court one with Gary

hal.thought_process: It's 9:17 on Saturday morning and the street is quiet. I've already logged the notebook, swept Magnolia Loop with the binoculars, and confirmed nothing's pending. Gary filed his paperwork, the flamingos are behind the hedge, and that's all settled. Rosa's dinner is tonight, so my job is to show up on time with the cornbread and the table. Nobody's in line-of-sight, so there's no one to talk to. No sense fussing over the notebook again. I'll settle in on the porch chair, keep an eye on the street, and let the morning pass before I start on the cornbread.

parameters.content: Sit on the porch with a cup of coffee and watch the quiet street

rosa.thought_process: It's 9:17 AM Saturday. At tick 178 I started prepping the main dish for tonight's dinner, and the long table is already set with the cloth and seating planned. Hal's cornbread, Donna's cobbler, and Gary's ice and chairs are covered, so my job is the main course. I'm alone in the house with no one to talk to, and everything has been arranged already. The best thing now is to keep cooking at the kitchen so dinner is ready and I'm not scrambling before five.

parameters.content: Keep prepping the main dish for tonight's dinner

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
